summary: FCRA § 1681b(b)(3); ICRAA § 1786.40; CCRAA § 1785.20.5 (alternative); Breach of Contract; Implied Covenant; Promissory Estoppel; Negligent Misrepresentation; Fraud / Concealment; UCL § 17200; Penal Code § 290.46(j)

counts.title: [PLEADED ON INFORMATION AND BELIEF] FCRA, 15 U.S.C. § 1681b(b)(3)(A) — against AT&T if a consumer report contributed to rescission; invites federal-question removal; Plaintiff confirms no report/rights notice arrived before 12:23 p.m.; § 1681b(b)(2) standalone disclosure reserved until the authorization package is in hand

[INDEPENDENT PATH] ICRAA, Civ. Code §§ 1786.40 and 1786.50 — against AT&T as user; vendor First Advantage is not a named defendant; same-day screen, no 1786.40 advice at rescission; §§ 1786.10 / 1786.22 inspection not yet demanded; 1786.16 reserved until the exact authorization package is in hand
[ALTERNATIVE] CCRAA, Civ. Code §§ 1785.20.5 and 1785.31 — if the First Advantage product was an ordinary consumer credit report rather than investigative; no copy or rights notice before 12:23
[ALTERNATIVE] Breach of Written Contract and Implied Covenant — Plaintiff accepted through Workday and began onboarding
[ALTERNATIVE] Promissory Estoppel — official offer, compensation, tentative start date, accepted onboarding, and reliance
[ALTERNATIVE] Negligent Misrepresentation — official offer after assessment period if AT&T already treated the Spanish result as disqualifying or lacked grounds to represent approval

[ALTERNATIVE / DISCOVERY DEPENDENT] Intentional Misrepresentation and Concealment — requires internal proof of knowledge, intent, reliance, and managing-agent involvement for corporate punitive damages
[DERIVATIVE / EQUITABLE] UCL § 17200 — unlawful, unfair, and fraudulent prongs; restitution limited to vested money/property and injunction subject to standing and adequate-remedy proof

[PLEADED ON INFORMATION AND BELIEF] Penal Code § 290.46(j) — last count on page one; two-hour chronology, First Advantage order, contemporaneous Megan's Law listing, and absence of required adverse-action notices; AT&T report is not attached; Lerma cannot be decided on the face of this complaint
[PRESERVED, NOT PLEADED] FEHA and Fair Chance Act — do not plead without CRD exhaustion/right-to-sue and supporting score or criminal-history-use evidence
